title: Luxor Temple
source: Retained exact archaeological identity,ordinary inspected pictures and standard viewer PMTiles/Mapzen terrain.
axis: +X southwest along the mapped colonnade;+Y up;+Z northwest. Native entrance is -X;the first court and entrance wings retain their offset axes.
identityStatus: Q319841/way1079039494 identifies the archaeological area only. Standard PMTiles multipart building52776574920845 defines the temple ranges and parallel colonnade strips;35185602195324 independently fixes Serapis. Named obelisk,Tripartite Shrine and Tetrastyl points fix their approximate centers. Native+X follows the mapped colonnade southwest,not the broader undirected archaeological rectangle.

orientationControl.basis: Two parallel long mapped colonnade strips define the126-degree raw east/south axis. The entrance photograph and named obelisk distinguish the northeast approach from the rear sanctuary. Individual front-court/pylon edges remain independently offset;not surveyed facing.

reconstruction.scope: Luxor principal exterior from ordinary pictures and standard PMTiles: distinct entrance wings, surviving obelisk, open courts, seven-pair colonnade, rear ranges, selected shrines and the independently mapped Abu el-Haggag mosque exterior. Fine reliefs, statue carving, hidden historic interiors and surveyed floors are omitted.

reconstruction.heightBasis: No mapped architectural heights in the selected controls. Pylons,obelisk,column/capital profiles,partial roofs,statues,small shrines and rear room survival use picture-guided medium-fi estimates. Column rhythms outside the pictured seven-pair colonnade are authored approximations,not a measured surviving inventory. Mosque body, raised floor, dome and two attached minarets use picture-guided estimates; the tall background New Mosque minaret is not included.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retained unmodified standard161-square/6m DEM. NativeY0 is sampled at the chosen colonnade entrance origin;piecewise neighborhood medians guide approximate floor grades. Covered floor polygons exclude the raised mosque foundation;boundary panels join the coarse terrain. No archaeological survey or bespoke terrain source.

mosqueExterior.identity: Abu el-Haggag mosque; independent PMTiles building 35184706301534
mosqueExterior.basis: Mapped footprint; raised white body, dome, tall white minaret and older tapered stone minaret from the inspected ordinary exterior photographs. All architectural heights and internal positions are estimates. The separate New Mosque minaret in the background is excluded.

reconstruction.rearSurvivalBasis: Mapped rear outline retained as surviving boundary wall bands, with open axial doorways, selected side partitions and partial roofs. Interior wall inventory and roof survival are medium-fi approximations; no solid reconstruction roof over the rear ruins.
